h1: Tube and profile laser cutting machines — Ø0.3″ to 25.2″, 20 to 40 ft tubes, 1.5 to 40 kW
intro: A tube laser cuts round, square, rectangular and open profiles to length and cuts the holes, copes, slots and notches in them in one pass — no saw, no drill, no notcher, no layout — straight from the 3D model. Every tube laser NovoTech sells in Canada is on this page, and the table below sets the series side by side: how many chucks, what tube, how long and heavy a bar, how fast, and how it is loaded. Two chucks hold the tube at both ends and leave a short tail on each bar — the Dener E-FTL made in Turkey, NovoTech's ULT, the Senfeng T series, the high-speed PLUS for small tube in volume and the GPLUS / GT that cut ±45° bevels. Three chucks cut the last part with zero tail and carry long, heavy tube: the Dener FTL to Ø25.2″, the ULT three-chuck, the Senfeng NT and the heavy ST to Ø25″ and 6,614 lb. Each machine can be loaded by hand or crane, or with a semi-automatic or fully automatic loader — explained below. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and tube nesting software, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Two or three chucks — which should I buy?
faq.a: By what you cut and what the leftover costs you. Two chucks hold the tube at both ends; the rear chuck has to keep hold of the bar, so a short tail of every bar is scrap — fine for mild steel in short and medium runs, and the cheapest machine: the Dener E-FTL, the NovoTech ULT and the Senfeng T, PLUS and GPLUS / GT. A third chuck takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut with zero tail, and it supports long, heavy tube so it is cut straight: the Dener FTL, the ULT three-chuck, the Senfeng NT and, for pipe and structural tube to Ø25″, the Senfeng ST. On 20 to 40 ft bars of stainless, aluminum or heavy-wall tube the saved material pays for the third chuck.

The premium Dener E-FTL and FTL are built in Turkey with servo-driven chucks (1 G on the E-FTL), a Maxphotonics fiber source, a BOCI autofocus head and ±0.05 mm repeatability, with parts stocked in Canada — for the shop that runs the tube laser all day. NovoTech's value-line ULT and the Senfeng T / PLUS / GT / NT / ST are built in China with pneumatic chucks, in a wider range of sizes and powers at a lower price; NovoTech stocks the parts and does the service. The premium machine is faster between parts and holds tighter tolerance at high duty.

The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust — Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, accelerating at 1 G and running 394 ft/min on the small chucks. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube and pipe to Ø25.2″ and 40 ft (12 m) bars of 5,732 lb (2,600 kg), with ±0.1 mm repeatability on the large chucks. Both take 3 to 20 kW sources. The E-FTL holds the bar in two chucks and leaves a tail of 1.4″ (35 mm) or more; the FTL's three chucks cut the last part with zero remnant. A fully automatic bundle loader is an option on the E-FTL, a semi-automatic loader on the FTL.

faq.q: What can a tube laser cut?
faq.a: Round, square, rectangular, oval and open profiles — angle, channel, flat bar — in mild steel, stainless, aluminum, copper and brass, from the chuck's minimum to its maximum size, in wall thicknesses to about 1/2″ (12 kW) or 3/4″ (20 kW). Holes, slots, copes for tube-to-tube joints, tabs and notches for folding, engraving — anything you can draw on the surface of the profile. A 5-axis or 45° bevel head adds weld preparations and mitred corners.

faq.q: Do I need an automatic loader?
faq.a: Not to start: every machine here is loaded by hand or crane as standard, and the loader can usually be added later. A semi-automatic loader is worth it once an operator spends more time lifting tube than watching the machine — the operator keeps a rack or chain filled and the loader feeds one tube at a time, open profiles and special shapes included. A fully automatic bundle loader takes a whole 3 t bundle from the crane and feeds round, square and rectangular tube with nobody at the machine — the choice for production runs and two shifts.

faq.q: What is zero-tailing — the NT series?
faq.a: A two-chuck machine cannot cut the last part of the bar because the rear chuck has to hold something, so a remnant of the chuck length is scrapped from every bar. The NT puts a third chuck in the middle that takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut and the tail is near zero — on 20 to 40 ft stock to Ø14″ that is several percent of material saved on every bundle.

The number is the largest round tube in millimetres: E-FTL 120 takes Ø0.3 – 4.7″, 180 to 7.1″, 250 to 9.8″ and 350 to 13.8″; FTL 250, 350, 500 and 640 take Ø0.6″ to 9.8, 13.8, 19.7 and 25.2″. Square and rectangular tube goes to the same size — 350 × 350 mm (13.8″) on the 350 chuck. Buy the chuck for the largest tube you cut regularly — a smaller chuck is faster and holds thin tube better — and the bar length — 23, 30 or 40 ft (7, 9 or 12 m) on the E-FTL, 20, 30 or 40 ft (6, 9 or 12 m) on the FTL — for the stock you buy.

faq.q: Can it cut bevels and weld preparations?
faq.a: Yes — the bevel (3D) head, standard on the 12 m FTL 12035, 12050 and 12064 and optional on the other FTL and E-FTL models, tilts the beam so mitred corners, chamfers and weld preparations are cut in the same pass as the holes and copes; the tube arrives at the welding table ready to fit. The seam detector orients welded tube so the seam sits where the drawing puts it.

The CNC imports STEP / IGES solid models of the tube parts, unfolds them onto the profile, nests them along the bar to use the remnant and writes the program — with the cutting database for the material and seam detection to orient welded tube. Offline programming on a PC is standard on both lines.

A 23 ft (7 m) machine needs about 65 ft (20 m) of length including the loader and unloader; a 40 ft (12 m) machine about 100 ft (30 m). 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas and a dust collector. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

loading.title: Loading the tube: by hand, semi-automatic or fully automatic
loading.lead: Every tube laser on this page can be loaded three ways. The loader does not change what the machine can cut — it decides how much of the operator's time each bar takes, and whether the machine keeps cutting while nobody stands at it.

cards.title: By hand or crane — no loader
cards.text: The operator lifts each tube onto the infeed supports — by hand for light tube, with a hoist or crane for heavy bars. The rear chuck pulls it in, the chucks centre and clamp it, the following supports carry it and the machine cuts the whole bar on its own; the finished parts drop onto the unloading rack.
items: Standard on the Senfeng T, PLUS, GPLUS / GT and NT, the NovoTech ULT and the Dener E-FTL and FTL
The lowest price and the shortest machine
Any profile the chucks hold — angle, channel and special shapes too
Right for short runs, mixed jobs and light tube

cards.title: Semi-automatic loader
cards.text: The operator lays a row of tubes on the loader's sloped rack or chains and keeps it filled; the loader separates one tube at a time, lifts it to the chuck centre and feeds it in. A tube outside the loader's size or weight is still loaded by hand.
items: Sloped loader: 17 – 20 ft (5.2 – 6.2 m) tubes up to 265 lb (120 kg) — round, square, rectangular and channel
Dual-arm chain loader: 13 – 20 ft (4 – 6.1 m) tubes up to 529 lb (240 kg) — also angle, channel and I-beam
Chain loader: 13 – 40 ft (4 – 12 m) tubes and profiles up to 1,543 lb (700 kg)
Takes special shapes and open profiles that a bundle loader cannot; included on the Senfeng ST

cards.title: Fully automatic bundle loader
cards.text: The crane sets a whole bundle — up to 3 t (6,600 lb) — into the loader; it separates the tubes, aligns each one and feeds it to the chuck with no operator, while the unloading system sorts the parts from the scrap. One person runs the machine and prepares the next bundle while it cuts, and the machine keeps cutting through breaks.
items: Fully automatic loader: 11.5 – 20 ft (3.5 – 6.1 m) tubes, 15 – 30 ft (4.5 – 9 m) on the 9 m machines
Simplified fully automatic loader: the same 3 t bundle on a lighter frame, also for 20 – 40 ft (6 – 12 m) tubes
Round, square and rectangular tube of standard section, 265 – 573 lb (120 – 260 kg) per tube
The choice for production runs and two-shift work

loading.note: Unloading: a 6.6 ft (2 m) unloading rack that sorts scrap from parts is standard on the Senfeng T and PLUS (10 or 13 ft optional) and a 10 ft (3 m) unloading system on the NT (20 ft optional). Dener E-FTL: a fully automatic loader is optional (the 120 and 180 chucks can also have a semi-automatic one); Dener FTL: a semi-automatic loader is optional; NovoTech ULT: a pneumatic loader for tube to Ø8.7″ or a bundle feeding system.
